n: As a storm seems to roll in, Elihu’s heart pounds and leaps at the sound.

f.g: Elihu may be describing a real storm approaching — the storm from which God will speak.

n: Listen to the thunder of God’s voice and the rumbling from his mouth!
He sends it across the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.

f.w: his lightning unto the ends of the earth

n: After the flash comes the roar; God thunders with majestic voice and doesn’t hold back the lightning.
God thunders wonderfully; he does great things beyond our understanding.

f.w: great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend

n: He tells the snow, “Fall on the earth,” and commands both light showers and heavy downpours.
In winter storms God brings all human work to a stop so that people will recognize his work.

f.w: He sealeth up the hand of every man
f.g: He halts human labor through bad weather.

n: Animals take shelter in their dens.
The storm comes from its chamber in the south, and cold from the scattering north winds.
By God’s breath ice forms and broad waters freeze solid.

f.w: By the breath of God frost is given

n: He loads the clouds with moisture and scatters his lightning through them.
The clouds swirl at his direction, carrying out everything he commands across the world.
God sends storms for different purposes — to correct, to water his land, or to show mercy.

f.w: whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy

n: Elihu calls on Job to stop and consider God’s wonders — just what God is about to ask Job to do.

f.w: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God

n: Does Job know how God orders the clouds or makes lightning flash?
Does he understand how clouds float in balance — the wonders of the One perfect in knowledge?

f.g: How clouds hang suspended in the air.

n: Job swelters in his clothes when the hot south wind stills the land.

f.g: The hot desert wind from the south.

n: Can Job, like God, spread out the sky, hard as a mirror of cast bronze?

f.g: A mirror of polished cast metal — ancient mirrors were bronze.

n: Tell us what to say to God — we can’t prepare a case because we are in the dark.
Should anyone tell God, “I want to speak”? Wouldn’t that be asking to be swallowed up? Elihu warns Job about demanding a hearing.

f.w: surely he shall be swallowed up

n: No one can look at the sun when it shines in the skies after the wind has swept the clouds away.

f.w: the bright light which is in the clouds
f.g: The sun, dazzling in a cleared sky.

n: Out of the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed in awesome majesty. Elihu’s speech ends just as God appears.

f.g: Literally “gold” — golden radiance, perhaps the glow of God’s glory.

n: We cannot reach the Almighty; he is great in power and justice and will not violate righteousness.

f.g: He does not oppress or pervert justice.

n: That is why people revere him; he does not regard those who think themselves wise. The stage is set for the Lord to speak.

f.w: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart
